sourceFacts.finding: Lexer is inside parser.ts. Grammar ends inputUnit at a top-level newline; semicolon/and-or lists, nested compounds, escaped newlines, quotes and pending heredocs stay parser-managed. Parser lookahead must not consume future words under the wrong alias state.
Accepted source already parses/executes successive units for exec, -c, streamed stdin, source and eval; later errors need not precede earlier effects.
scriptFile precollects all units; parseShell is whole-input; command substitutions contain pre-parsed Script ASTs, unlike default Bash5.3 deferred alias reading.

State and cloneState have no alias/shopt state. Functions store Command bodies and run with current state; isolated execution/substitution/invoke clones; processState creates fresh state. Source/eval use current state. Anchors here use accepted CD464, not LET-shifted lines.

Accepted glob method uses compilePattern, per-segment leading-dot filtering, VFS signal, bounded fields/bytes/work, sorting and literal unmatched fallback. No dotglob switch or explicit dot/dot-dot guard; no adapter semantics inferred.

Public parser is parseShell; exec takes string, not AST. Internal Runtime accepts ASTs. Function display depends on spelling. Literal invocation, shared budgets and lifecycle contracts remain constraints.

verifiedOfficialSectionUrls.fact: Edition/version 5.3, last updated 18 May 2025; blank means space or tab.

Unquoted command-position words are replaced with shell input while reading; active-name recursion suppression and trailing-blank next-word eligibility apply. Complete lines/compounds/functions are read before execution; noninteractive expansion needs expand_aliases.
Definitions, reusable listings, named queries and removals have actual behavior and missing-name failures; unalias -a removes all.

Set/unset, reusable/ordinary listings and quiet all-enabled queries are distinct. Listing status reflects enabled options; setting unknown names fails. dotglob defaults off; expand_aliases defaults on only interactively; globskipdots defaults on.
Leading dots require explicit matching unless dotglob; dot and dot-dot still require leading-dot patterns, and globskipdots excludes them even then. Slash remains explicit.
Aliases and shopt settings belong to the shell execution environment.
POSIX mode always enables aliases and expands them during initial command-substitution parsing; default non-POSIX mode generally defers enabled alias expansion until substitution execution.
